story: On a warm Monday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is cruising along Magnolia Loop in his golf cart, cheerfully promising Hal that he'll be at Rosa's by six and that the parade wiring is finally finished. Hal, leaning wryly against his own cart, reminds him that the Architectural Review paperwork should have gone in before the wiring, not after. Meanwhile, Donna is heading off, determined to track Gary down, while Rosa, back at the Rec Center and a little harried, asks her to pass along the six o'clock reminder and a friendly pardon for the disposal.
events: Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: I just finished zip-tying the cart wiring and fitting fuses, so the build is nearly done. My memories say I need to be at Rosa's by six and not let anyone down again, and it's only 3:17, so there's time. Hal is right here and was kind to me when I showed up late last time. A quick friendly word is a good way to say thanks and to ask about the parade. I don't need to file anything new since the cart form is already in. I'll keep it short and natural.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Hal. Thanks again for not giving me grief about being late to Rosa's. I'm on my way over by six this time, and the cart's wiring is finally buttoned up for the parade.

donna.thought_process: Rosa already answered me about dinner, so I shouldn't ask again. My real problem is Gary has vanished and we're on the ladder now. He's probably not at the Rec Center, since only Rosa is here. Time to go look for him instead of standing around chatting. Magnolia Loop is the only way out, and he might be heading home before dinner.

parameters.content: Heading out to track down my doubles partner before dinner.

hal.thought_process: I'm at the bulletin board's street with Gary just arrived beside me. I already read the notices last tick, and I promised Rosa I'd show up at six sharp with something in hand. Gary's cart wiring and Donna's flamingos still bug me, but I've been keeping a ledger of everyone's mistakes and it's wearing thin. Gary did say he'd file the paperwork after wiring, which is backwards. A short, firm word is my duty, but I can keep it civil and then go get on with my afternoon.

parameters.content: Gary, the paperwork goes in before the wiring, not after. Get your cart mods in front of Architectural Review before that parade and we'll have no trouble, you and me.

rosa.thought_process: Donna just asked if I've seen Gary. I haven't since way back at tick 2, when he and Donna ran off for coffee. I already invited her to dinner at six, so no need to repeat that. The useful thing is to answer her honestly, point her toward where Gary might be, and tell her to pass the dinner word along if she finds him. The ladder standings board is right here, so she may be able to track him down that way.

parameters.content: Haven't laid eyes on Gary since this morning, hon. If you track him down, remind him six sharp at my place, and tell him the disposal is long forgiven.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
